### **Overview**

This is an assignment to create two useful functions, one that creates a plot, one that does something else. 2 examples per function are shown as evidence of the functions' flexibility.

### **Load Libraries**

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(DT) #interactive table to fully view output of function 1
library(leaflet) #interactive map for function 2
```

### **Load Data**

I am using data from the Sherwood et al. 2025 paper - [Systematics and taxonomy of *Codium* (Bryopsidales, Chlorophyta) in the Hawaiian Islands: Description of six new species](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/jpy.70091). Specifically, I'm using the [collection information of Hawaiian *Codium* specimens](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/action/downloadSupplement?doi=10.1111%2Fjpy.70091&file=jpy70091-sup-0016-TableS1.docx) analyzed in this study, to illustrate the collection locations of characterized specimens belonging to each clade/taxon of Hawaiian *Codium*.

To show the functions' flexibility, I am also using data from the Allsopp et al. 2026 paper - [Three new species of *Scinaia* (Scinaiaceae, Nemaliales) from Hawaiian mesophotic reefs](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00318884.2026.2653264). Specifically, I'm using the [collection information of Hawaiian *Scinaia* specimens](https://www.tandfonline.com/action/downloadSupplement?doi=10.1080%2F00318884.2026.2653264&file=uphy_a_2653264_sm6137.xlsx) analyzed in this study, to illustrate the collection locations of characterized specimens belong to each clade/taxon of Hawaiian *Scinaia*.

```{r}
Codium <- read_csv(here("Week_08", "Data", "Codium_collection_data.csv"))   #Data for the genus Codium
Scinaia <- read_csv(here("Week_08", "Data", "Scinaia_collection_data.csv")) #Data for the genus Scinaia
```

### **Load Functions**

#### [Function 1: Assign marker colors to each taxon]{.underline}

This function automatically assigns predefined Leaflet marker colors to each unique taxon in a dataset column. This adds the assigned colors as a new marker_color column.

**Usage: assign_taxon_colors(\
data,\
taxon_column\
)**

```{r}
assign_taxon_color <- function(
    data,           #Data frame containing taxon records and information
    taxon_column) { #Column containing taxon names
  
  #The 19 predefined marker colors supported by Leaflet awesomeIcons()
  available_colors <- c(
    "red", "darkred", "lightred", "orange", "beige",
    "green", "darkgreen", "lightgreen", "blue", "darkblue",
    "lightblue", "purple", "darkpurple", "pink", "cadetblue",
    "gray","lightgray","black" #Omitted "white" because marker icon will be white
  )
  
  #Extract the column specified by taxon_column from the dataset
  taxa <- unique(data[[taxon_column]]) #Get all unique taxa in that column
  taxa <- sort(taxa[!is.na(taxa)])     #Remove NA and sort remaining taxon names alphabetically
  
  #Assign a marker color to each unique taxon
  taxon_colors <- setNames(         #Uses taxon names as names for their corresponding colors
    rep(available_colors,           #Repeat the 19 available colors as many times as needed
        length.out = length(taxa)), #Sets the total number of colors to match the number of taxa
    taxa
  )
  
  #Add a new column named marker_color to the original dataset
  data <- data |> 
    mutate(
      marker_color = unname( #Removes the names from the resulting color vector so mutate() inserts only the color values into marker_color
        taxon_colors[as.character(.data[[taxon_column]])] #Converts the taxon values to character strings so they match the names used in taxon_colors
      )
    )
  
  #Return the modified dataset, including the new marker_color column
  return(data)
}
```

#### [Function 2: Generate individual interactive distribution maps for each taxon]{.underline}

This functions generates a list of interactive Leaflet maps, with one map per taxon. Each map displays specimen collection locations on satellite imagery, using color-coded markers, italicized taxon labels, and popups containing specimen information. The function accommodates optional data columns and automatically adjusts the map extent to display the taxon's recorded locations.

**Usage: create_taxon_maps(\
data,\
taxon_column,\
longtitude_column,\
latitude_column,\
location_column,\
date_column,\
color_column,\
authority_column = NULL,\
type_column = NULL,\
collector_column = NULL,\
depth_column = NULL\
)**

```{r}
#Define a function to create one interactive map for each taxon
create_taxon_maps <- function(
    data,                    #Data frame containing taxon records and information
    taxon_column,            #Column containing taxon names
    longtitude_column,       #Column containing longitude coordinates
    latitude_column,         #Column containing latitude coordinates
    location_column,         #Column containing collection locations
    date_column,             #Column containing collection dates
    authority_column = NULL, #Optional column containing taxonomic authority
    type_column = NULL,      #Optional column containing specimen type information
    collector_column = NULL, #Optional column containing collector(s) names
    depth_column = NULL,     #Optional column containing collection depths
    color_column = NULL) {   #Optional column containing marker colors for each record
  
  #Identify all unique taxa, excluding missing taxon names
  taxa <- unique(data[[taxon_column]]) #Get all unique taxa in that column
  taxa <- taxa[!is.na(taxa)]           #Remove NAs
  
  #Create an empty list to store the individual taxon maps
  maps <- list()
  
  #Loop through each unique taxon to generate its own map
  for (taxon in taxa) {
    
    #Filter the dataset to include only the current taxon
    taxon_data <- data |> 
      filter(.data[[taxon_column]] == taxon)
    
    #Create leaf-shaped map markers using the assigned color for each record
    taxon_icons <- awesomeIcons(
      icon = "ion-leaf",                       #Use a leaf-shaped icon
      library = "ion",                         #Use the Ionicons icon library
      iconColor = "white",                     #Set the icon symbol to white
      markerColor = taxon_data[[color_column]] #Set marker colors from the specified column
    )
    
     #Create the initial popup text for each specimen record
      popup_text <- paste0(
        "Taxon: <i>", taxon_data[[taxon_column]], "</i>",  #Includes taxon name (italicized)
        "<br>Location: ", taxon_data[[location_column]],   #Includes collection location
        "<br>Collection Date: ", taxon_data[[date_column]] #Includes collection date
      )
    
     #Add taxonomic authority only if an authority column is provided
     if (!is.null(authority_column)) {
       popup_text <- paste0(
         popup_text,
         ifelse(is.na(taxon_data[[authority_column]]), "", #Omit if value is missing
                paste0("<br>Authority: ", taxon_data[[authority_column]]))
       )
     }
    
     #Add specimen type only if a type column is provided
     if (!is.null(type_column)) {
       popup_text <- paste0(
         popup_text,
         ifelse(is.na(taxon_data[[type_column]]), "", #Omit if value is missing
                paste0("<br>Type: ", taxon_data[[type_column]]))
       )
     }
    
     #Add collector information only if a collector column is provided
     if (!is.null(collector_column)) {
       popup_text <- paste0(
         popup_text,
         ifelse(is.na(taxon_data[[collector_column]]), "", #Omit if value is missing
                paste0("<br>Collector: ", taxon_data[[collector_column]]))
       )
     }
    
     #Add collection depth only if a depth column is provided
     if (!is.null(depth_column)) {
       popup_text <- paste0(
         popup_text,
         ifelse(is.na(taxon_data[[depth_column]]), "", #Omit if value is missing
                paste0("<br>Depth: ", taxon_data[[depth_column]], "m"))
       )
     }
    
    
    
    #Initialize an interactive Leaflet map using the filtered taxon data
    taxon_map <- leaflet(taxon_data) |> 
      addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) |> #Add Esri satellite imagery as map background
      fitBounds( #Automatically adjust map extent to include all records for the taxon
        lng1 = min(taxon_data[[longtitude_column]], na.rm = TRUE) - 0.1,
        lat1 = min(taxon_data[[latitude_column]], na.rm = TRUE) - 0.1,
        lng2 = max(taxon_data[[longtitude_column]], na.rm = TRUE) + 0.1,
        lat2 = max(taxon_data[[latitude_column]], na.rm = TRUE) + 0.1
        #Add 0.1 degrees of padding to each boundary to prevent excessive zooming
      ) |> 

      #Add interactive markers for the current taxon's specimen locations
      addAwesomeMarkers(
        lng = taxon_data[[longtitude_column]], #Set marker longitudes
        lat = taxon_data[[latitude_column]],   #Set marker latitudes
        icon = taxon_icons,                    #Apply the colored leaf icons
        
        #Display the taxon name in italics when hovering over a marker
        label = ~lapply(
          paste0("<i>", taxon_data[[taxon_column]], "</i>"),
          htmltools::HTML
        ),
        
        #Display the corresponding specimen information when a marker is clicked
        popup = ~lapply(popup_text, htmltools::HTML)
      )
    
    #Store the completed map in the list, using the taxon name as its key
    maps[[as.character(taxon)]] <- taxon_map
  }
  
  #Return the named list containing all individual taxon maps
  return(maps)
}
```

### **Test Functions**

#### [Function 1: Assign marker colors to each taxon]{.underline}

#### *Codium* dataset

```{r}
#Assign marker colors to each Codium taxon (18 total)
Codium_color <- assign_taxon_color(
  Codium,  #Dataset containing Codium records
  "Taxon") #Column containing taxon names

datatable(Codium_color) #Interactive table to fully view output
```

#### *Scinaia* dataset

```{r}
#Assign marker colors to each Scinaia taxon (4 total)
Scinaia_color <- assign_taxon_color(
  Scinaia,   #Dataset containing Scinaia records
  "Species") #Column containing taxon names

datatable(Scinaia_color) #Interactive table to fully view output
```

#### [Function 2: Generate individual interactive distribution maps for each taxon]{.underline}

#### List of maps generated for *Codium* dataset.

```{r}
#Generate individual interactive maps for each Codium taxon (18 total)
Codium_maps <- create_taxon_maps(
  Codium_color,   #Dataset containing Codium records and marker colors
  "Taxon",        #Column containing taxon names
  "Long",         #Column containing longitude coordinates
  "Lat",          #Column containing latitude coordinates
  "Island",       #Column containing collection location information
  "Date",         #Column containing collection dates
  "Authority",    #Column containing taxonomic authority information
  "Type",         #Column containing specimen type information
  "Collector",    #Column containing collector(s) names
  "Depth",        #Column containing collection depths
  "marker_color") #Column containing assigned marker colors

#Display the names of all taxa for which maps were created
names(Codium_maps)
```

#### A specific *Codium* map

```{r}
#Display the interactive map for a specific Codium taxon
Codium_maps[["Codium cf. arabicum"]]
```

#### All *Codium* maps

```{r}
# Display all Codium maps
htmltools::tagList(
  lapply(names(Codium_maps), function(taxon) { #Loop through the names of all taxa with available maps
    htmltools::tagList(                        #Create a heading and display the corresponding taxon's map
      htmltools::tags$h4(                      #Add the taxon name as a level-four heading
        htmltools::tags$em(taxon)),            #Italicized the taxon name
      Codium_maps[[taxon]]                     #Retrieve and display the map associated with the current taxon
    )
  })
)
```

#### List of maps generated for *Scinaia* dataset.

```{r}
#Generate individual interactive maps for each Scinaia taxon (4 total)
Scinaia_maps <- create_taxon_maps(
  Scinaia_color,  #Dataset containing Scinaia records and marker colors
  "Species",      #Column containing taxon names
  "Longitude",    #Column containing longitude coordinates
  "Latitude",     #Column containing latitude coordinates
  "Location",     #Column containing collection location information
  "Date",         #Column containing collection dates
  NULL,           #No taxonomic authority column is available
  "Type",         #Column containing specimen type information
  "Collectors",   #Column containing collector(s) names
  "Depth",        #Column containing collection depths
  "marker_color") #Column containing assigned marker colors

#Display the names of all taxa for which maps were created
names(Scinaia_maps)
```

#### A specific *Scinaia* map

```{r}
#Display the interactive map for a specific Scinaia taxon
Scinaia_maps[["Scinaia uohulualii"]]
```

#### All *Scinaia* maps

```{r}
# Display all Scinaia maps
htmltools::tagList(
  lapply(names(Scinaia_maps), function(taxon) { #Loop through the names of all taxa with available maps
    htmltools::tagList(                         #Create a heading and display the corresponding taxon's map
      htmltools::tags$h4(                       #Add the taxon name as a level-four heading
        htmltools::tags$em(taxon)),             #Italicized the taxon name
      Scinaia_maps[[taxon]]                     #Retrieve and display the map associated with the current taxon
    )
  })
)
```
